requirements.evidence: Contract matches: CallMode enum (app/Enums/CallMode.php:5-9), NoWaitingTicketsException extends RuntimeException (app/Exceptions/NoWaitingTicketsException.php:7), invokable action with the required signature (app/Actions/CallNextTicket.php:20). Queue row locked and is_active read from the locked row (:25-32); candidate locked and re-checked with skip list (:45-54); ordering priority desc/issued_at/id (:92-96); normal_only oldest first (:76-79); fairness with last 3 by called_at desc, id desc and fallback when no normal waits (:85, :102-115); only status/called_at/called_by_user_id written and the updated model returned (:56-61). Small risk: fairness history filters on status = Called (:106), so tickets that later move to another status (if the lifecycle has one) would drop out of 'last 3 tickets called'; called_at IS NOT NULL alone would match the rule.

conventions.evidence: Domain write lives in app/Actions as one invokable class; docs/business-rules.md and docs/architecture.md updated as required (diff lines 190-208, 237-253); CHANGELOG updated under [Unreleased]. Deviations: the same CHANGELOG entry is also added to the already released [0.0.0] section (CHANGELOG.md:39), and the public __invoke has no PHPDoc describing the exceptions it throws.

security.evidence: Authorization is out of scope by the task (caller trusted) and the docs say so explicitly (docs/architecture.md:206). No mass assignment: fields are set individually (app/Actions/CallNextTicket.php:56-59). Queue state comes from the database under lock, not from the client-supplied model (:25-32). No user input or output rendering is involved.

tests.evidence: tests/Feature/CallNextTicketTest.php covers full ordering including the id tie-break (:46-56), returned/persisted state (:58-70), other queues and no re-call (:72-82), NoWaitingTickets for each mode (:84-93), inactive queue with stale model and no changes (:95-103), mode filters (:105-115), fairness trigger and reset (:117-130), no normal waiting (:132-139), priority_only calls counted in history (:141-154), fewer than 3 calls / normal in last 3 (:156-172), called_at tie broken by id (:174-184), and the concurrent-skip path simulated with a retrieved hook (:186-200).

simplicity.evidence: Lean, single action with three small private helpers and no extra layers. pickCandidate uses two closures plus a nested ternary with ?? fallback (app/Actions/CallNextTicket.php:76-87), which is compact but a bit clever for what are three straightforward queries.

readability.evidence: Clear names (pickCandidate, byFullOrdering, mustCallNormal, FAIRNESS_WINDOW) and useful comments on locking (app/Actions/CallNextTicket.php:23-24, :34-35). Minor noise: unused $normal variables in the test (tests/Feature/CallNextTicketTest.php:157, :165), and the ternary with ?? inside a match arm (:84-86) takes a second read.

scope.evidence: All new files and doc edits serve the task. The only stray edit is the duplicated CHANGELOG entry inserted into the released [0.0.0] section (CHANGELOG.md:39), which misstates release history.

issues.explanation: The new entry is duplicated into the already released [0.0.0] section; it should appear only under [Unreleased].

Fairness history filters on status = Called, so if tickets later move to another status (served, etc.) they would drop out of the 'last 3 tickets called' window; filtering on called_at IS NOT NULL would match the rule more robustly.
The public __invoke has no PHPDoc documenting the modes and the InactiveQueueException/NoWaitingTicketsException it throws.
$normal is assigned but never used (also at line 165).
The nested ternary with a ?? fallback inside the match arm is harder to read than a short if block.

review.summary: Adds CallMode, NoWaitingTicketsException and the CallNextTicket action with queue/ticket locking, deterministic ordering, mode filtering, the 3-priority fairness rule and skip-on-concurrent-call, plus thorough Pest tests and updated docs. The implementation meets the contract and rules; the remaining issues are minor (a CHANGELOG entry duplicated into a released section, a status-based history filter that could be fragile, small readability nits), so it is approvable with nits.
